question: How do I set up my Fern documentation to be hosted on a custom subdomain like docs.mydomain.com?
ground_truth: To host your Fern documentation on a custom subdomain, you need to: 1) Update your docs.yml file to add the custom-domain field with your subdomain, 2) Contact Fern via Slack or email to receive a unique CNAME value and TXT record for domain verification, 3) Create DNS records in your domain registrar including a CNAME record pointing your subdomain to the provided value and a TXT record for verification, and 4) Wait for DNS propagation and SSL provisioning to complete.

metadata.cited_context: To host your documentation on a subdomain like `docs.mydomain.com`, you need to create a CNAME record in your DNS settings. Add your `custom-domain` and merge your changes into `main`. Contact Fern via your dedicated Slack channel or email to receive: A unique CNAME value for your site, A TXT record to verify your domain. Log in to your domain registrar's dashboard and navigate to the DNS settings for your domain. Add the following records: CNAME Record (Subdomain) Type CNAME Name docs Value b7278b3c9357963d.vercel-dns-013.com, TXT Record (Domain Verification). Once Fern has completed your setup, you'll be able to access your documentation at `docs.mydomain.com`. SSL will be automatically provisioned for your domain.
